primitives.name: Local Stationarity Approximation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Core trick: approximate the non-stationary process at each time t by a stationary process sharing the same causal structure (Dahlhaus-style local stationarity, Props 1–2), then estimate per-time-point DAGs with a kernel-localized M-estimator (Epanechnikov, bandwidth via quasi-k-fold CV) using NOTEARS (linear) or NTS-NOTEAR (nonlinear) losses.

primitives.breakdown_regime: When global non-stationarity dominates or kernel smoothing fails due to insufficient data.

reasoning_traces.think:
DYNAMO addresses the core challenge of inferring causal relationships in non-stationary environments by introducing a framework that assumes local stationarity around each time point. It constructs a sequence of stationary approximations to the global process, enabling estimation of time-varying directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) through kernel-weighted M-estimation. This approach avoids standard assumptions such as stationarity, faithfulness, and constant Gaussian noise, making it suitable for modeling complex systems like football matches where referee behavior, crowd dynamics, and player performance vary over time. The method uses a loss function defined over a sliding window of observations weighted by an Epanechnikov kernel, optimizing causal structures at each time step. In GSI context, this supports Bayesian updating of beliefs about home advantage mechanisms, while in GSE, it enables dynamic modeling of team performance evolution based on causal drivers like officiating trends and fan presence. The key insight is that even in non-stationary settings, local causal structures remain stable enough to permit reliable inference.
